note: FAILED by the preregistered rule: the 95 percent interval of the bird offset d (0.330 to 0.455) lies wholly above 0.30, so birds use about 2.5 times more energy per gram over their lifespan than mammals of the same mass. The mass slope s = -0.114 (interval -0.140 to -0.088) also misses the PASS band but does not by itself meet the FAIL rule. Reported checks agree (mammals only -0.108; captivity records only d = 0.416). Scope: this removes the author-declared scope 'individual lifespan = one reserve per gram / metabolic rate' (rate-of-living); it does not touch tau = F/P for closed reserves (starvation, hibernation) or the layer-3 abundance law N = b tau. UET-distinct failure: current biology already rejects rate-of-living, so the null does not fail. Not blind (literature known). Intervals are too narrow because there is no phylogenetic correction; d is about 0.09 above the threshold, about 1.5 times the half-width of its interval.
